items.item_text: Experience developing multichannel communications, including email, web, social media, and/or print.
Experience using CRM platforms, analytics tools, or digital engagement systems to inform strategy.

The External Relations Specialist, Annual & Special Gifts Program serves as an experienced professional responsible for developing and implementing complex alumni engagement and annual giving initiatives for the Annual & Special Gifts Program (ASGP). This position plans, develops and implements strategies for specific programs, events, policies, constituency groups, while advancing ASGP’s goals.

The External Relations Specialist independently engages in day-to-day alumni relations operations and participates in the creation of innovative engagement and fundraising programs and initiatives. This position collaborates with internal partners to maximize outreach, execute annual giving outreach initiatives, and constituent connections. The External Relations Specialist works within the central development office to create and execute annual giving and stewardship efforts, and key engagement events, including digital campaigns and initiatives such as Give Day and Crowdfund UC Davis. This position collaborates with fundraising staff and managers to design and implement a comprehensive alumni engagement program in alignment with institutional priorities and the strategic goals of the Annual & Special Gifts Program. The External Relations Specialist provides leadership in improving business processes, recommending policy or procedural enhancements, and developing training related to alumni relations operations.
This position requires good judgment in selecting methods and techniques for obtaining solutions, and works collaboratively, and collegially as part of a large, matrix organization.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of training and experience.

Demonstrated experience providing and managing administrative and logistical support for programs, events, or projects and executing programs or events with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and complex logistics.

Experience with planning, coordinating, and executing complex programs or events in a service-oriented environment using professionalism, tact, and discretion. Ability to independently manage complex events or initiatives, anticipate issues, and resolve problems diplomatically and effectively.

Experience developing and delivering written and verbal communications for external audiences, including correspondence, event messaging, stewardship materials, or digital content. Experience evaluating program or event outcomes and using data, feedback, or trends to inform improvements.
Demonstrated research, analytical, and critical thinking skills, including the ability to assess complex situations, identify risks or opportunities, and recommend effective solutions.
Demonstrated ability to translate constituent interests, motivations, and institutional priorities into effective engagement, stewardship, and communication strategies.
Demonstrated skill in project management, including planning, organizing, prioritizing, and executing programs or events while meeting deadlines and maintaining attention to detail.
Familiarity with industry best practices in alumni relations, annual giving, constituent engagement, or stewardship.

Awareness, knowledge, and skill in applying inclusion to one’s work. A profound belief in the value of a safe workforce and a commitment to achieve this goal through collaboration and team building, working cooperatively with a large group of department and campus constituencies.
